To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the D1 receptor and muscarinic receptor regulate adenylate cyclic synthesis in the NS20Y neuroblasts by interacting with the stimulatory and inhibitory guanine nucleotide regulatory proteins, respectively, and that cholera toxin treatment of NS20Y cells activates the adenylate cyclate system by increasing the sensitivity of adenylate cyalse to forskolin, and by causing the accumulation of cAMP in the cells.
cholera toxin, but not pertussis toxin, activates the adenylate cyclases in the NS20Y cell.

the D1 receptor and the muscarinic receptors are coupled to adenylate cyclases via Gs and Gi, respectively, and that cholera toxin stimulates the activity of Gs, which in turn stimulates the activity of adenylate cylcase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of guanine nucleotide regulatory proteins (GNRP) in the modulation of cyclic AMP synthesis by D1 dopamine and m1 muscarinic receptors in NS20Y rat neuroblastoma cells.
the role that guanine nucleotide (GTP) binding proteins play in the regulation of cAMP synthesis in NS20y neuroblastoma cells.
the mechanisms by which dopamine and muscarine regulate cyclic AMP accumulation in NS20Y cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the D1 dopamine receptors in these neuroblastoma cells activate adenylate cyclases through a Gs protein, whereas the muscarinic receptors inhibit adenylate cyclates through a Gi protein.
cholera toxin activates adenylate cyclases through Gs and Gi, whereas pertussis toxin inhibits adenylate cyclates through Gi.
cholera toxin, pertussis, toxin, forskolin and D1 dopamine receptors are involved in the regulation of cAMP synthesis in NS20 Y cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
D1 dopamine receptors and muscarinic cholinergic receptors on NS20y neuroblastoma cells are coupled to adenylate cyclases via distinct G-proteins.
the G-proteins are a class of proteins that bind to GTP and GDP.
the D1 receptor stimulates adenylate cyclate through a G-protein, while the muscarinic receptor inhibits adenylate cyclatse through another G-protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to show the effects of cholera toxin in the neuroblastoma cells.
the D1 agonist dihydrexidene is able to increase cAMP in NS20Y cells, and this effect is additive with the effects of cholera toxin, which activates a stimulatory guanine binding protein, Gs.

the D1 dopamine receptor and the muscarinic acetylcholine receptor are coupled to the adenylate cyclases through different guanine nucleotide-binding proteins (G-proteins) in these neuroblastoma cells.
